question: Identify the most critical clauses (NI=3) across all regulations and their subdomain coverage
cypher: MATCH (c:Clause {normativeIntensity: 3})-[:MAPPED_TO]->(sd:SubDomain) RETURN c.clauseId AS clauseId, c.regulationId AS regulation, c.description AS clauseDescription, sd.subDomainId AS subDomainId, sd.name AS subDomainName, sd.gapRisk AS gapRisk, sd.soleAuthority AS soleAuthority ORDER BY c.normativeIntensity DESC, c.regulationId, c.clauseId;

data.clauseDescription: Risk management system for high-risk AI: continuous, iterative process throughout lifecycle.
Risk management measures: identify, analyse and estimate known and foreseeable risks of high-risk AI.
Special category data in training: strict minimization; only where strictly necessary and with safeguards.
Logging capabilities: automatic recording of events throughout the lifetime of the high-risk AI system.
Logs must enable monitoring of AI system operation with respect to occurrence of situations that may present risk.
Retain logs for period appropriate to intended purpose; at least 6 months where applicable.
Instructions for use: identity of provider, characteristics, capabilities, limitations, performance metrics.
Human oversight: high-risk AI designed to be effectively overseen by natural persons during period of use.
Human oversight measures: persons assigned must have competence, training and authority to intervene.
Resilience against adversarial manipulation: protection against data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial inputs.
Automatically generated logs: provider shall keep AI system logs (Art. 12(1)) for at least 6 months.
Quality management system: written policies, procedures covering all aspects of high-risk AI compliance.
QMS includes procedures for design control and verification; regular assessment of effectiveness of measures.
QMS includes examination, test and validation procedures; risk management documentation.
Deployer assigns human oversight to persons with necessary competence, training and authority.
Post-market monitoring system: proactively collect and review data on performance of high-risk AI in real world.
Reporting of serious incidents: providers report to market surveillance authorities within prescribed timelines.
Market surveillance: authorities verify compliance; test AI systems against regulatory requirements.
GPAI models with systemic risk: adversarial testing; model evaluation against state-of-the-art benchmarks.
GPAI systemic risk: report serious incidents and possible corrective measures to AI Office without delay.
No known exploitable vulnerabilities at delivery; products designed with no known exploitable vulnerabilities.
Secure by default configuration; product delivered in most secure default state.
Secure default configuration: disable unused ports, services, interfaces; no default passwords.
Security updates: product can receive security updates, including automatic update mechanisms.
Protection of integrity: no unauthorised manipulation of data, commands or configuration.
Secure and verifiable updates: authentication of updates; cryptographic integrity verification.
Vulnerability identification and documentation: identify and document components; produce SBOM.
Software Bill of Materials: document all third-party components and dependencies in machine-readable format.
Address vulnerabilities without delay: remediate vulnerabilities promptly; share information on fixes.
Coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy: publish policy; responsible disclosure process.
Manufacturer obligation: design, develop and produce products in accordance with Annex I requirements.
Cybersecurity risk assessment: undertake and document assessment before placing product on market.
Technical documentation: maintain documentation demonstrating conformity for 10 years after placing on market.
Notify actively exploited vulnerability to CSIRT/ENISA: early warning within 24h; notification within 72h.
Notify severe incidents impacting security of product: report to ENISA and relevant CSIRTs.
Management body responsible for ICT risk management framework; board accountability for ICT risk.
Management body members keep up-to-date knowledge of ICT risk; regular training on digital resilience.
Sound, comprehensive and well-documented ICT risk management framework approved by management body.
ICT risk management framework: document all ICT risks; assess likelihood and impact of risk scenarios.
Identify and classify all ICT assets: hardware, software, data assets and ICT-related processes.
ICT asset management: changes to ICT assets documented; configuration management for all assets.
Continuously identify all sources of ICT risk including third-party exposure; implement detection tools.
Identify and assess vulnerabilities in ICT systems; document and track all identified vulnerabilities.
Protection of confidentiality and integrity: encryption of sensitive data at rest.
Protection of data in transit: encryption of data during transmission across networks.
Protection of integrity and availability of data: prevent unauthorised modification of data and systems.
Logging mechanisms: log all ICT-related activities; ensure traceability of operations and access.
ICT systems updates: policies and procedures for timely patching of vulnerabilities; update management.
Access control: limit logical and physical access to ICT assets; need-to-know and least privilege.
Access management: dedicated management of access rights including provisioning and deprovisioning.
Strong authentication mechanisms including multi-factor authentication for all critical systems.
Cryptographic key protection: secure management of keys used for authentication and data protection.
ICT security policies: implement security into ICT systems design and architecture from the outset.
ICT security policies for software development: secure development practices; code security standards.
Anomaly detection mechanisms: continuously monitor ICT systems for anomalous behaviour and threats.
Early warning indicators: mechanisms to identify and detect ICT-related incidents in real time.
Response and recovery: ICT business continuity policy; procedures to respond and recover from incidents.
Backup policies: tested backup procedures; recovery time and recovery point objectives defined.
Incident response plans with defined roles, communication protocols and escalation procedures.
Data and system restoration methods: documented and regularly tested procedures to restore operations.
Classify ICT-related incidents: classification criteria including client impact, data loss, service disruption.
Report major ICT-related incidents to competent authority: initial notification, intermediate and final report.
Digital operational resilience testing programme: regular testing of all ICT tools and systems.
Testing of ICT tools, systems and processes using scenario-based tests, vulnerability assessments.
ICT third-party risk management: general principles; risk-based assessment of all ICT providers.
Concentration risk assessment: identify and manage risk from critical ICT third-party provider concentration.
Key contractual provisions with ICT providers: mandatory security clauses in all ICT service contracts.
Contractual rights of access, inspection and audit over ICT third-party service providers.
Right to erasure: controller must erase personal data on request.
Right to data portability: data subject receives data in structured, machine-readable format.
Data Processing Agreement: mandatory contractual clauses binding the processor to security obligations.
Records of processing activities: controller and processor maintain written records of all processing.
Breach notification to supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware.
Documentation of all personal data breaches, including facts, effects and remedial action taken.
Breach notification to data subject when breach likely to result in high risk to rights and freedoms.
Data Protection Impact Assessment mandatory prior to high-risk processing operations.
DPIA must include systematic description of processing and purposes, necessity assessment, risk assessment.
Designation of Data Protection Officer where required by scale/nature of processing.
Management body approval and oversight of risk management measures; accountability at board level.
Management body members must undergo cybersecurity training; ensure sufficient knowledge to govern risks.
Risk analysis and information system security policies: documented, board-approved security policies.
Multi-factor authentication or continuous authentication solutions as mandatory baseline.
Early warning to CSIRT or competent authority without undue delay and within 24 hours of awareness.
Incident notification within 72 hours including initial assessment of severity and impact.
Final incident report within one month: detailed description, type of threat, root cause, cross-border impact.
Significant incident determination: entities must classify incidents by impact on service continuity.
